title: Fresh Margherita Pizza
subtitle: Basil, mozzarella, blistered crust
description: Basil, mozzarella, blistered crust. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Fresh Margherita Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Proof dough for blistered crust
steps.instruction: Bloom yeast in warm water 5 minutes. Mix flour, salt, oil, and yeast water; knead 8–10 minutes until smooth. Rise 1–1½ hours until doubled. Margherita needs relaxed gluten for leopard spotting on the rim.

steps.title: Make quick tomato sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer crushed tomatoes with smashed garlic 12 minutes until slightly thickened. Season lightly with salt — fresh mozzarella brings salt too. Cool briefly; hot sauce melts dough.

steps.title: Heat stone to maximum practical temp
steps.instruction: Preheat stone or steel at 500°F at least 45 minutes. Drain mozzarella on paper towels and slice evenly — wet cheese makes a soggy center.

steps.title: Stretch, light sauce, mozzarella only
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inch rounds. Sauce sparingly — red should peek through cheese. Arrange mozzarella slices in one layer with slight overlap. No toppings yet; basil goes on after the bake.

steps.title: Bake for leopard spots
steps.instruction: Bake 9–12 minutes until crust is spotted brown and cheese has melted with a few golden blisters. Rotate once. Underbaked Margherita tastes like cheese on raw bread — look for color on the underside.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Fresh Margherita Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Basil, olive oil, rest, and cut
steps.instruction: Immediately scatter whole basil leaves and drizzle olive oil. Finish with flaky salt. Rest 2 minutes, cut into 8 slices. Fresh Margherita Pizza — tomato, mozzarella, basil. Serve fast; basil wilts on a hot hold.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Fresh Margherita Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Basil, mozzarella, blistered crust. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Fresh Margherita Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
